newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Deadline for UGB unions on Hoogovens deal.
newsitem.headline: Deadline for UGB unions on Hoogovens deal.

text.p: LA LOUVIERE, Belgium, Jan 24 - Belgian steelmaker Usines Gustave Boel SA (UGB), which is negotiating an alliance with Dutch steel group Hoogovens, said on Friday that if unions did not agree to a social plan including job cuts within 48 hours, it would apply for bankruptcy.

UGB spokesman Pierre Stievenart told Reuters that there was a 48-hour ultimatum. If there was no union deal before it expired, UGB management would hand over company records to a local commercial court, effectively filing for bankruptcy.
UGB's work council was in an extraordinary meeting on Friday to discuss the situation.
The alliance with Hoogovens envisages reducing UGB's workforce to 1,200 in the first quarter of 1997 from the current level of around 2,000.
Hoogovens aims to take a 50 percent stake and invest three billion Belgian francs in UGB if there is an accord to restructure the company which is family-owned.
Unions rejected the plan in December.
